17 year old sculptress Vinnie Ream with her marble bust of President Lincoln which she used to win the commission for a full size statue for the Capitol Rotunda. D.C. 1864

Vinnie Ream (1847 – 1914) was an American sculptor. Her most famous work is the statue of Abraham Lincoln in the U.S. Capitol rotunda.

Ream was one of the first women to be employed by the federal government, as a clerk in the dead letter office of the United States Post Office from 1862 to 1866 during the American Civil War. In 1863 she became an apprentice in Clark Mills's sculpting studio and in 1864, President Lincoln agreed to model for her each morning for five months and she created a bust of his figure. She used this bust of Lincoln as her entry into the selection contest for a full-size sculpture.

Ream became the youngest artist and first woman to receive a commission as an artist from the United States government for a statue in 1866 when she was awarded the commission for the full-size Carrara marble statue of Lincoln by a vote of Congress on July 28, 1866, when she was 18 years old. In 1871 the statue was unveiled in the United States Capitol rotunda when Ream was only 23 years old.
